newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Vishay Israel unit starts new chip output.
newsitem.headline: Vishay Israel unit starts new chip output.

text.p: Vishay Israel Ltd said its plant in Dimona, southern Israel, has begun production of a newly-patented electronic power resistor chip.
Vishay Israel is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Vishay Intertechnology. Since its introduction last year the chip had been produced only in Vishay's U.S. plants.

Chairman and CEO of Vishay Intertechnology Felix Zandman said the first customers to use the new resistor chip for lithium batteries are Japanese companies Sony, Matsushita Communication and Sanyo Industries.
The company declined to disclose the value of the deals.
Zandman said the market for power chip resistors is estimated at $150 million.

"Our sales of this product are already running at a rate of $15 million and production capacity is presently sold out. Manufacturing this product in Israel will provide us with lower costs due to lower taxes and grants, hence placing the company in a better position to meet future competition," Zandmann said.

Pennsylvania-based Vishay Intertechnology has sales of $1.2 billion. Vishay Israel has three manufacturing facilities in Israel. Sales are running at an annual rate of $300 million, 95 percent of which is for export.
